tasks.title: Port .NET conventions into csharp-style, dotnet and efcore fragments
acceptance: The three fragments exist and are within their contract budgets (fragments.md §1): `wc -l .sir/disciplines/csharp-style.md .sir/disciplines/dotnet.md .sir/disciplines/efcore.md` reports csharp-style.md ≤ 110, dotnet.md ≤ 220, efcore.md ≤ 40 lines. Base: No such file.

Self-contained (discussion.md E1; DoD D3): `grep -nE 'backend-conventions|dotnet-format|dotnet-guidelines|frontend-conventions|playwright-guidelines|react-format|react-guidelines|vitest-guidelines' .sir/disciplines/csharp-style.md .sir/disciplines/dotnet.md .sir/disciplines/efcore.md`, run from the worktree root, prints nothing and exits 1 — no line of csharp-style.md, dotnet.md or efcore.md names any of the 8 convention docs. Base: the files do not exist (grep exits 2), so not vacuous. Control that must stay unchanged by this task: `grep -lE 'backend-conventions|dotnet-format|dotnet-guidelines|frontend-conventions|playwright-guidelines|react-format|react-guidelines|vitest-guidelines' docs/backend-conventions.md docs/dotnet-format.md docs/dotnet-guidelines.md docs/frontend-conventions.md docs/playwright-guidelines.md docs/react-format.md docs/react-guidelines.md docs/vitest-guidelines.md` prints exactly docs/backend-conventions.md, docs/dotnet-format.md, docs/frontend-conventions.md, docs/react-format.md (measured at 2e0f9e2). Reviewer also confirms by reading that no fragment defers a rule to any external document instead of stating it inline.

Each fragment is a rule list, not a tutorial (sir-disciplines, "The format": rules stated imperatively and checkable by reading a diff): every rule is an imperative bullet or table row; prose that only motivates a rule is cut; a fenced example appears only where it shows a layout rule prose cannot state unambiguously.

Each fragment holds only its contract topic (fragments.md §1): csharp-style.md states only rules binding every C# file, test files included (naming, file organization, layout, XML documentation); efcore.md states only data-access rules; everything else from T1's units is in dotnet.md. Reviewer reads all three.

Every C# example in T1's fragments uses a descriptive lambda parameter (memory convention M2, fragments.md §5 precedence over the single-letter examples at docs/dotnet-format.md:243 and docs/dotnet-guidelines.md:141): every line `grep -nE '\b[a-z] =>' .sir/disciplines/csharp-style.md .sir/disciplines/dotnet.md .sir/disciplines/efcore.md` prints is an example explicitly labelled as the incorrect form. Base: files absent.
